title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tajikistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Tajikistan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Tajikistan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Because Tajikistan's domestic statutory and agency portals are only partially accessible online or in English, this guide combines verified international statutory archives (WIPO Lex, CIS Legislation, FAOLEX, and HCCH) with accessible Tajik government portals and UK consular guidance [1] [2] [6] [8]. We set out the five main steps below for medical certification, civil registration at ZAGS, burial or repatriation, succession within the six-month deadline, and Hague Apostille legalization [1] [5] [6] [7].

steps.title: Secure the medical death certificate and register the death
steps.html:
• Obtain the medical notification of death: Under Tajikistan's Law on State Registration of Acts of Civil Status (Law No. 2117 of January 2, 2025, which superseded the 2006 Law No. 188), civil registration requires a medical certificate of death issued by a hospital, clinic, mortuary, or forensic medical body, or an enforced court judgment establishing death [1] [2] [7].
  • Report within three days at ZAGS: Spouses, family members, witnesses, or treating institutions submit the written declaration to the local Civil Registry Office (ZAGS, supervised by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan) [1] [2] [10]. Statutory rules expect reporting within three days of death or discovery of the body, although late reporting cannot be refused, and ZAGS normally issues official certificates (in Tajik and Russian) on the day of application or within 1 to 3 days [2] [7].
  • Bring required identity records: Present the deceased's passport (ZAGS may retain a foreign national's passport to forward through Migration Services and diplomatic channels if buried locally), proof of kinship, and a notarized Power of Attorney if a funeral director or agent applies [7].

steps.title: Arrange burial, repatriation, and Hague Apostille certification
steps.html:
• Confirm local burial or transfer abroad: Local funeral arrangements proceed once ZAGS issues the death certificate; families planning international repatriation need embalming, non-infectious disease clearance, customs permits, and diplomatic coordination [7].
  • Check post-mortem protocols: Forensic examination is mandatory in sudden, unexplained, or external deaths and can extend certificate timelines if cause of death remains under investigation [7].
  • Apostille documents for use outside Tajikistan: Tajikistan has been a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention since 31 October 2015 [6]. Under HCCH Competent Authority rules, the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan apostilles civil registry certificates (ZAGS death, birth, and marriage records) and notarial or court acts, whereas the Main Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostilles educational and archive records, at a statutory fee equal to 75 percent of one calculation indicator [6] [8].

steps.title: Notify pension, social protection, and banking bodies
steps.html:
• Report to social protection and pension authorities: Inform local branches of the Ministry of Health and Social Protection of the Population (and the Agency for Social Insurance and Pensions) with the ZAGS death certificate so pension payments stop cleanly and any survivor benefits or statutory burial support can be reviewed [9] [11].
  • Request extra certified copies and Russian/Tajik extracts: ZAGS and consular offices regularly expect multiple originals; staff primarily operate in Tajik or Russian, so retain a qualified translator where needed [7].
  • Notify banks and employers: Inform banks so accounts are safeguarded until formal succession documents are presented, and settle final employment wages or insurance claims [4] [5].

steps.title: Open inheritance proceedings within six months
steps.html:
• Observe the six-month acceptance window: Under Part Three (Section VI: Succession Law) of the Civil Code of the Republic of Tajikistan (together with the updated Civil Code framework in Law No. 1918 of December 24, 2022), succession opens on the date of death and heirs must apply to accept the estate at a state notary office within six months [3] [4] [5].
  • Verify wills and statutory heirs: Notaries check for any written notarized will and identify statutory heirs by priority order, issuing a Certificate of Right to Inheritance after the six-month term expires [5].
  • Appoint a local proxy if abroad: Heirs residing outside Tajikistan should execute a written Power of Attorney, apostilled under the 1961 Convention and translated into Tajik or Russian with notarial certification [6] [7].

steps.title: Re-register property titles and address tax or debt rules
steps.html:
• Transfer real estate and vehicles: Present the notarized Certificate of Right to Inheritance to municipal property registration bureaus and tax offices before selling or leasing inherited property [4] [5].
  • Confirm estate obligations: Under Civil Code succession rules, heirs who accept an estate succeed to documented assets alongside outstanding debts only within the limits of inherited estate value [4] [5].

closingQuestion: In which city or region of Tajikistan did your family member live, and will any heirs need apostilled documents for proceedings abroad?

contacts.name: Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Tajikistan
contacts.note: Supervises Civil Registry Offices (ZAGS), state notaries handling inheritance files, and Apostille certification for civil status, notarial, and judicial records.

contacts.name: Main Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
contacts.note: Apostilles archive and educational documents, handles foreign passport return notices, and coordinates diplomatic legalization or repatriation matters.

contacts.name: Ministry of Health and Social Protection of the Population
contacts.note: Oversees public hospitals, forensic medical examiners issuing death notifications, and social protection and pension administration.
